scope.basis: Current-run public/discovery evidence and normalized requirements only.
scope.coverage_note: Discovery and inventory contain 25 URLs, including partial collections; SEO page-level observations below are restricted to the URLs and artifacts explicitly cited. No Google Search Console, index coverage, ranking, or field performance evidence was available.

findings.title: The advertised sitemap endpoints return 404
findings.observation: Both /sitemap.xml and /pub/sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404 in this run. robots.txt advertises https://addp.vn/pub/sitemap.xml. This establishes failure at these sampled endpoints during collection; it does not establish whether a sitemap is available at another URL.
findings.suggested_direction: Investigate the published sitemap location and its HTTP response; update the robots.txt Sitemap directive if the canonical sitemap endpoint differs.
unknowns: Whether another sitemap URL is valid.
Whether crawlers have an alternate discovery source or cached sitemap.
Actual search-engine discovery or indexing impact.

planning.objective: Make the sitemap location advertised to crawlers resolve to a valid sitemap response.
planning.target_state: The advertised sitemap URL returns a parseable sitemap with an appropriate successful status.
recommended_changes: Verify the intended public sitemap URL.
Correct the sitemap endpoint or the robots.txt Sitemap directive.
developer_investigation: Determine the intended sitemap endpoint and confirm response status and XML content.
acceptance_criteria: The sitemap URL advertised in robots.txt returns a valid sitemap response.
automated_verification: GET advertised sitemap URL and validate status and XML.
manual_verification: Inspect sitemap URL set for intended public URL coverage.
risks: Changing sitemap location without checking existing crawler-facing configuration could leave stale discovery references.

findings.title: Robots policy uses a broad wildcard rule and advertises an unavailable sitemap
findings.observation: The collected robots.txt contains a single User-agent: * group with Disallow: /*? and lists the /pub/sitemap.xml endpoint, which returned 404 in this run. No named AI user-agent groups appear in the collected file. The wildcard query-string disallow may restrict crawl access to parameterized URLs; actual effect is URL/rule specific.
findings.suggested_direction: Review whether query-string URLs that should be crawled are covered by /*?, and align the advertised sitemap URL with an endpoint that responds successfully. Confirm intended AI crawler policy explicitly before adding or changing user-agent directives.
unknowns: Which parameterized URLs are intended to be discoverable.
Whether the site intends to allow all named AI crawlers; absence of dedicated groups alone does not establish a block under the wildcard rule.
Actual crawler behavior and indexed URL effects.

planning.objective: Keep crawl directives and sitemap discovery aligned with intended public URL access.
planning.target_state: Robots directives permit intended crawlable URLs and point to a working sitemap.
recommended_changes: Review query-string disallow scope against representative parameterized URLs.
Confirm AI crawler policy and document any agent-specific directives if needed.
developer_investigation: Compare disallowed URL patterns with intended canonical and crawlable URL types.
acceptance_criteria: Robots rules match the confirmed crawl policy and advertise a responding sitemap endpoint.
automated_verification: Parse robots directives and check representative URLs against the intended policy.
manual_verification: Review policy for Googlebot and requested AI crawler user agents.
risks: Broad robots changes can expose or suppress URL classes unintentionally.

findings.title: Sampled product pages have missing or generic meta descriptions
findings.observation: The raw SEO extraction for /sui-dovital reports meta_description as ‘Default Description’. The other two sampled priority product detail pages have descriptions matching their product title rather than a distinct summary: /1goi-sua-hat-dinh-duong-glucare-plus.html and /vien-an-duong-addp.html. These are three sampled product URLs, not a sitewide prevalence estimate.
findings.suggested_direction: Write a product-specific meta description for each sampled detail page, replacing the default value and avoiding simple title duplication.
unknowns: Whether search engines currently display these descriptions or rewrite them.
Metadata quality and uniqueness on uncollected product URLs.

planning.objective: Provide a distinct, accurate search-result summary for each sampled product page.
planning.target_state: Each sampled product URL exposes a unique, descriptive meta description aligned with visible page content.
recommended_changes: Review whether the descriptions on the two named product pages need expansion beyond the title.
developer_investigation: Check page-level metadata configuration for the sampled product records.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed page returns a unique, non-default description that accurately summarizes its visible content.
automated_verification: Extract meta descriptions for the three URLs and compare for default values and duplicates.
manual_verification: Review descriptions for accuracy and usefulness as search-result summaries.
risks: Descriptions must remain consistent with the visible product claims and page content.

rubric.item: Title, meta description, canonical, and robots metadata
rubric.scope: Page instances only; metadata observations are sampled and do not establish sitewide coverage

rubric.item: Headings and rendered internal link signals
rubric.scope: Sampled page instances; no sitewide pattern asserted

rubric.item: Robots directives, sitemap discovery, and AI user-agent policy
rubric.scope: Sitewide public endpoint observations; crawler effects and AI access intent unknown

rubric.item: JSON-LD / structured data on sampled homepage and product pages
rubric.scope: Page instances; collector reports valid=0 and invalid=0, interpreted as no detected JSON-LD in those captures; not all structured-data formats
Three page instances; each capture reports one valid and zero invalid items; no sitewide coverage claim

rubric.scope: Page instances; artifact pair comparison sufficient to inspect selected pages only, and cannot establish server rendering for all text, prices, or descriptions sitewide

rubric.item: Search-engine indexing, Search Console status, and rankings
rubric.scope: Sitewide outcome; no direct evidence available

rubric.item: Broken linked resources and link target response health
rubric.scope: Link count and failed resource counts do not establish broken internal link targets; comprehensive target-response audit unavailable

rubric.item: Mobile render and metadata signals relevant to indexability
rubric.scope: Mobile captures for these page instances only; not a mobile indexability verdict

rubric.item: Canonical completeness on sampled partial pages
rubric.scope: Page instances; observed extracted canonical is null, but partial collection prevents interpreting this as confirmed missing source metadata

strengths.observation: The homepage exposes a self-referencing canonical and INDEX,FOLLOW robots metadata in the raw capture.
The three sampled article pages each expose a canonical matching the requested URL and each collected article structured-data capture reports one valid item and zero invalid items.

unknowns: Actual Google or other search-engine indexing, rankings, traffic, and Search Console data were not present in current-run artifacts.
Field Core Web Vitals and field performance are unavailable; collected Lighthouse-style metrics are LAB and not treated as FIELD.
Sitemap availability at paths other than the two tested endpoints is unknown.
Comprehensive broken internal-link target status is unknown; observed failed resource signals are not equivalent to broken links.
The collector's structured-data count does not establish support or absence of every non-JSON-LD structured-data format.
